title: Finite-type quasi-coherent submodules extend across a qc open
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] which is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $U\subseteq X$ be an open subscheme which is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. For an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal M$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and an open $W\subseteq X$ write $\mathcal M|_W$ for its restriction ($\mathcal M|_W(T)=\mathcal M(T)$ for opens $T\subseteq W$); a *submodule* $\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal M$ is a sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module, i.e. $\mathcal G(T)\subseteq\mathcal M(T)$ is an $\mathcal O_X(T)$-submodule for every open $T$, compatibly with restriction, and $\mathcal G$ is a sheaf. Let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent] and let $\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal F|_U$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-submodule which is of finite type [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]. Then there is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-submodule $\mathcal G'\subseteq\mathcal F$ of finite type with $\mathcal G'|_U=\mathcal G$ as submodules of $\mathcal F|_U$, i.e. $\mathcal G'(T)=\mathcal G(T)$ for every open $T\subseteq U$.

proof.text: *A finite affine cover.* By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] every point of $X$ has an affine open neighbourhood, so the affine opens cover $X$; since $X$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], there are finitely many affine opens $V_1,\dots,V_n$ ($n\ge0$) with $X=U\cup V_1\cup\dots\cup V_n$. Put $W_0=U$ and $W_k=U\cup V_1\cup\dots\cup V_k$. Every $V_k$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], and a finite union of quasi-compact subsets is quasi-compact, so every $W_k$ is a quasi-compact open of $X$, and $W_n=X$.

*Affine case, first part: a quasi-coherent extension.* In this and the next three steps fix a quasi-compact open $W\subseteq X$, an affine open $V\subseteq X$, put $W_V=W\cap V$, and let $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal F|_{W_V}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{W_V}$-submodule of finite type; we construct a quasi-coherent submodule $\mathcal K'\subseteq\mathcal F|_V$ of finite type with $\mathcal K'|_{W_V}=\mathcal K$. Since $V$ is affine it is quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], and since $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated its underlying space is spectral [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral], so the intersection of two quasi-compact opens of $X$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-spectral-space]; hence $W_V$ is quasi-compact. The inclusion $j:W_V\to V$ is quasi-compact: an affine open $T\subseteq V$ is an affine open of $X$, hence quasi-compact, and $j^{-1}(T)=W\cap T$ is quasi-compact by the same property of $X$. The $\mathcal O_V$-module $\mathcal F|_V$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits] (2). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-extension-qc-open] to $j$, $\mathcal F|_V$, $\mathcal G=\mathcal K$ and the inclusion $\varphi:\mathcal K\to\mathcal F|_{W_V}$: there are a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_V$-module $\mathcal H_0$, an $\mathcal O_V$-linear $\psi:\mathcal H_0\to\mathcal F|_V$ and an isomorphism $\alpha:\mathcal H_0|_{W_V}\to\mathcal K$ with $\varphi\circ\alpha=\psi|_{W_V}$. Let $\mathcal H=\operatorname{Im}\psi\subseteq\mathcal F|_V$ (sections locally in the image of $\psi$); it is a quasi-coherent submodule by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] (1), (2). Its definition is local, so for an open $T\subseteq W_V$, $\mathcal H(T)$ is the set of sections of $\mathcal F(T)$ locally in the image of $\psi|_{W_V}=\varphi\circ\alpha$; as $\alpha$ is an isomorphism this image is $\mathcal K$ (locally, hence, $\mathcal K$ being a sheaf, $\mathcal H(T)=\mathcal K(T)$). Thus $\mathcal H|_{W_V}=\mathcal K$.

*Affine case, second part: local finite generation.* Let $R=\mathcal O_X(V)$ and identify $V$ with $\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $N=\mathcal H(V)$; by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] (3) the counit $\widetilde N\to\mathcal H$ is an isomorphism, so by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] for every $f\in R$ we have $\mathcal H(D(f))\cong N_f$ as $R_f$-modules, $n/f^k\mapsto f^{-k}\,n|_{D(f)}$. Let $u\in W_V$. The principal opens $D(f)$ form a basis of the Zariski topology ($\operatorname{Spec}R\setminus V(I)=\bigcup_{f\in I}D(f)$), so there is $f\in R$ with $u\in D(f)\subseteq W_V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion] $D(f)$ is the image of the open immersion $\operatorname{Spec}R_f\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, so $D(f)$ is an affine open of the scheme $W_V$ with $\mathcal O(D(f))=R_f$. The restriction $\mathcal K|_{D(f)}$ is of finite type (restrict the local generating sections of [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation] (1) to the smaller opens; an epimorphism of sheaves stays one on a smaller open), so by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine] (a), applied to the scheme $W_V$, the quasi-coherent module $\mathcal K$ and the affine open $D(f)$, the $R_f$-module $\mathcal K(D(f))=\mathcal H(D(f))\cong N_f$ is finitely generated. Since $W_V$ is quasi-compact (step 2), finitely many such $D(f_1),\dots,D(f_m)\subseteq W_V$ cover $W_V$, and $N_{f_i}$ is generated by finitely many elements, which after multiplying numerators and denominators by powers of $f_i$ we write $x_{i,1}/f_i^e,\dots,x_{i,r_i}/f_i^e$ with $x_{i,j}\in N$ and one exponent $e$.

*Affine case, third part: the finite type submodule.* Let $N'\subseteq N$ be the $R$-submodule generated by all $x_{i,j}$; it is finitely generated. By the adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] (1) there is a unique $\mathcal O_V$-linear $\beta:\widetilde{N'}\to\mathcal H$ with $\beta_V\circ\tau_V$ equal to the inclusion $N'\subseteq N=\mathcal H(V)$. The module $\widetilde{N'}$ is quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] with $\widetilde{N'}(V)\cong N'$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] (2) finitely generated, so it is of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine] (a) (applied to the affine open $V$ of the scheme $V$). Let $\mathcal K'=\operatorname{Im}\beta\subseteq\mathcal H\subseteq\mathcal F|_V$. It is a quasi-coherent submodule by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] (1), (2), and of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-image-extension] (1), as the image of a morphism whose source $\widetilde{N'}$ is of finite type.

*Affine case, fourth part: $\mathcal K'|_{W_V}=\mathcal K$.* Fix $i$ and write $D_i=D(f_i)$. For each $j$, the section $\beta_{D_i}(\tau_{D_i}(x_{i,j}))=\beta_V(\tau_V(x_{i,j}))|_{D_i}=x_{i,j}|_{D_i}$ lies in $\mathcal K'(D_i)$, which is an $\mathcal O(D_i)=R_{f_i}$-submodule of $\mathcal H(D_i)$; hence $\mathcal K'(D_i)$ contains $f_i^{-e}x_{i,j}|_{D_i}$, which corresponds to the generator $x_{i,j}/f_i^e$ of $N_{f_i}$ under $\mathcal H(D_i)\cong N_{f_i}$ (step 3). So $\mathcal K'(D_i)=\mathcal H(D_i)$. The restrictions $\mathcal K'|_{D_i}\subseteq\mathcal H|_{D_i}$ are quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits] (2) on the affine scheme $D_i\cong\operatorname{Spec}R_{f_i}$ [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion], and the inclusion $\iota:\mathcal K'|_{D_i}\to\mathcal H|_{D_i}$ is bijective on global sections. By naturality of the counit in [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] (1), $\iota\circ\varepsilon_{\mathcal K'|_{D_i}}=\varepsilon_{\mathcal H|_{D_i}}\circ\widetilde{\Gamma(\iota)}$, where both counits are isomorphisms by (3) and $\widetilde{\Gamma(\iota)}$ is an isomorphism as the image of one under a functor; so $\iota$ is an isomorphism, i.e. $\mathcal K'|_{D_i}=\mathcal H|_{D_i}=\mathcal K|_{D_i}$ (step 2). Finally the $D_i$ cover $W_V$: for an open $T\subseteq W_V$ and $s\in\mathcal K(T)$, every $s|_{T\cap D_i}$ lies in $\mathcal K'(T\cap D_i)$, so $s\in\mathcal K'(T)$ because $\mathcal K'$ is a subsheaf of the sheaf $\mathcal F|_V$; symmetrically $\mathcal K'(T)\subseteq\mathcal K(T)$. Hence $\mathcal K'|_{W_V}=\mathcal K$.

*One extension step (gluing).* Claim (E): if $W\subseteq X$ is a quasi-compact open, $V\subseteq X$ an affine open, and $\mathcal G_W\subseteq\mathcal F|_W$ a quasi-coherent submodule of finite type, there is a quasi-coherent submodule $\mathcal G''\subseteq\mathcal F|_{W\cup V}$ of finite type with $\mathcal G''|_W=\mathcal G_W$. Indeed $\mathcal K=\mathcal G_W|_{W\cap V}\subseteq\mathcal F|_{W\cap V}$ is quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits] (2) and of finite type (restriction, as in step 3), so steps 2–5 give a quasi-coherent submodule $\mathcal K'\subseteq\mathcal F|_V$ of finite type with $\mathcal K'|_{W\cap V}=\mathcal G_W|_{W\cap V}$. For an open $T\subseteq W\cup V$ put $\mathcal G''(T)=\{s\in\mathcal F(T): s|_{T\cap W}\in\mathcal G_W(T\cap W),\ s|_{T\cap V}\in\mathcal K'(T\cap V)\}$. This is an $\mathcal O_X(T)$-submodule, stable under restriction, and a sheaf (a section of $\mathcal F$ glued from sections of $\mathcal G''$ satisfies both conditions because $\mathcal G_W$ and $\mathcal K'$ are sheaves). For $T\subseteq W$ and $s\in\mathcal G_W(T)$ we have $s|_{T\cap V}\in\mathcal G_W(T\cap V)=\mathcal K'(T\cap V)$ as $T\cap V\subseteq W\cap V$; hence $\mathcal G''|_W=\mathcal G_W$, and in the same way $\mathcal G''|_V=\mathcal K'$. Quasi-coherence [pqf-def-coherent] (1) and finite type [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation] (1) are conditions on a neighbourhood of each point; every point of $W\cup V$ lies in $W$ or in $V$, where $\mathcal G''$ restricts to $\mathcal G_W$ or $\mathcal K'$, which satisfy them on open neighbourhoods inside $W$ resp. $V$. So $\mathcal G''$ is quasi-coherent of finite type.

*Induction on the number of affines.* With $W_k$ as in step 1 we show: for $k=0,\dots,n$ there is a quasi-coherent submodule $\mathcal G_k\subseteq\mathcal F|_{W_k}$ of finite type with $\mathcal G_k|_U=\mathcal G$. For $k=0$ take $\mathcal G_0=\mathcal G$. If $\mathcal G_{k-1}$ is constructed, apply (E) of step 6 to the quasi-compact open $W=W_{k-1}$, the affine open $V=V_k$ and $\mathcal G_W=\mathcal G_{k-1}$: it gives $\mathcal G_k\subseteq\mathcal F|_{W_k}$ quasi-coherent of finite type with $\mathcal G_k|_{W_{k-1}}=\mathcal G_{k-1}$, hence $\mathcal G_k|_U=(\mathcal G_k|_{W_{k-1}})|_U=\mathcal G_{k-1}|_U=\mathcal G$ since $U\subseteq W_{k-1}$. As $W_n=X$, $\mathcal G'=\mathcal G_n$ is the required submodule of $\mathcal F$.

split_report.summary: Split Stacks Properties 01PF into seven steps following its proof: a finite cover X = U ∪ V_1 ∪ … ∪ V_n by affines; the affine case in four steps (a quasi-coherent extension H ⊆ F|_V of K over the quasi-compact W ∩ V, taken as the image of the map given by 01PE(3) [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-extension-qc-open]; local finite generation of N = H(V) on principal opens D(f_i) by 01PB [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine]; N' generated by the numerators and K' = Im(N'~ → H) quasi-coherent of finite type; K' = H = K on each D(f_i) by the counit, hence on W ∩ V); the gluing step written out as an explicit subsheaf; and the induction on the number of affines with the inductive claim stated. Statement: finite type now cites def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation, quasi-compactness def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, and 'submodule' and restriction are spelled out. No new nodes: every lemma used exists; quasi-compactness of intersections of quasi-compact opens comes from the leaves lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral and def-weil-spectral-space, so the proof stays inside the route of sk-thm-p1 (no tool use of pqf-lem-qs-intersection-qc).
